newsitem.title: HUNGARY: HUNGARY'S CREDITANSTALT SIGNS 3-YR $90 MLN LOAN.
newsitem.headline: HUNGARY'S CREDITANSTALT SIGNS 3-YR $90 MLN LOAN.

text.p: Hungary's Creditanstalt Rt (CA), a subsidiary of Austria's Creditanstalt Bankverein, signed an agreement with a consortium of banks on Monday to take up a $90 million loan for three years.

The loan was priced at 17 basis points above LIBOR, the lowest interest rate provided to a Hungarian commercial bank to date, officials of Creditanstalt and loan arranger Bankgesellschaft told the signing ceremony.
"The 17 basis point above LIBOR is really a benchmark," Gerhard Richter of Bankgesellschaft Berlin said. "It's almost reaching the level of Italian banks."

Creditanstalt originally planned to take up $50 million, but on seeing the strong oversubscription decided to raise the loan to $90 million, said Creditanstalt Rt's Deputy General Manager Agnes Doffek.
The loan was provided by a 16-member consortium of west European banks.
Creditanstalt posted a pre-tax profit of 1.9 billion forints in the first half of 1997, up 36 percent from the same period of last year.
Its balance sheet total grew to 157 billion forints by the end of June, compared to 116 billion at the end of 1996.
Doffek said the bank was continuing its expansion in Hungary and expected the number of branches to rise to 20 by the end of 1997 from the current 14.
